pharm: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate that binds hydroxyapatite in bone and inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.
quick: One 150 mg tablet once monthly on the same date each month
Take in AM after an overnight fast; nothing but plain water for 60 min after
Not indicated; no human data; animal periparturient/fetal toxicity
Not indicated; no human milk data; present in rat milk
No specific interaction; avoid if it worsens GI symptoms
Serum calcium/vitamin D, dental status, thigh/groin pain, GI symptoms
summary: Ibandronate sodium is a nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate taken as a single 150 mg oral tablet once monthly for the treatment and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis. It increases bone mineral density and reduces vertebral fractures by inhibiting osteoclastic bone resorption. Strict administration is required to maximize absorption and avoid esophageal injury: take in the morning after an overnight fast with plain water, remain upright for at least 60 minutes, and wait at least 60 minutes before food, other beverages, or other medications. Notable risks include osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femoral fractures, and severe musculoskeletal pain. It is contraindicated with esophageal emptying abnormalities, hypocalcemia, inability to remain upright, and is not recommended when CrCl is below 30 mL/min.
indications: Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women
Prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women

dosage.t: Same date each month, in the morning
dosage.n: Take after overnight fast; reconsider continued therapy after 3-5 years in low-fracture-risk patients

dosage.d: Supplemental calcium and vitamin D if dietary intake inadequate

admin: Take one 150 mg tablet once monthly on the same date each month, in the morning
Swallow whole with 6 to 8 oz of plain water while standing or sitting upright; do not chew or suck
Take at least 60 minutes before the first food, drink (other than plain water), or any oral medication/supplement of the day
Do not lie down for at least 60 minutes after dosing to reduce esophageal irritation
Avoid mineral water and calcium-containing supplements within 60 minutes of the dose

If a dose is missed and the next scheduled day is more than 7 days away, take one 150 mg tablet the next morning, then resume the original schedule; if only 1-7 days away, skip and wait for the next scheduled day
moa: Ibandronate has a high affinity for hydroxyapatite in the bone mineral matrix. It inhibits osteoclast activity, reducing bone resorption and turnover. In postmenopausal women, lowering the elevated rate of bone turnover produces a net gain in bone mass and increased bone mineral density.

absolute: Esophageal abnormalities that delay emptying (e.g., stricture, achalasia)
Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 60 minutes
Known hypersensitivity to ibandronate or excipients (anaphylaxis reported)
relative: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) - use not recommended
Active upper GI disease (Barrett esophagus, dysphagia, esophagitis, gastritis, ulcers)
Invasive dental procedures or poor oral hygiene (osteonecrosis of jaw risk)
monitor: Serum calcium and vitamin D status (correct hypocalcemia before starting)
New or worsening upper GI symptoms (dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, heartburn)
Thigh or groin pain (possible atypical femoral fracture)

preg: Ibandronate is not indicated for use in women of reproductive potential. There are no human data to inform drug-associated risks. In animal studies it caused post-implantation loss, obstruction of labor, and maternal/fetal periparturient mortality, and renal developmental toxicity in offspring at exposures at or above the human once-monthly dose. Periparturient mortality appears to be a bisphosphonate class effect related to inhibition of skeletal calcium mobilization causing hypocalcemia and dystocia.
lact: Ibandronate is not indicated for use in women of reproductive potential. There is no information on its presence in human milk, effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production. Ibandronate is present in rat milk at concentrations averaging about 1.5 times plasma; the clinical relevance is unclear.
renal: Renal clearance is linearly related to creatinine clearance. Patients with CrCl less than 30 mL/min have more than a two-fold increase in exposure; ibandronate sodium tablets are not recommended for use in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min). No specific adjustment is provided for mild to moderate impairment.
hepatic: No studies have been conducted in hepatic impairment because ibandronate is not metabolized in the liver. No dosage adjustment is provided.

moderate: Calcium, antacids, and multivalent cations (aluminum, magnesium, iron): impair absorption - separate by at least 60 minutes
Aspirin and NSAIDs: additive GI irritation - use caution
minor: H2 blockers (ranitidine): ~20% increase in ibandronate bioavailability, not clinically relevant
interactions.food: Food and beverages other than plain water markedly reduce absorption (~90% reduction with a standard breakfast); take after an overnight fast and wait at least 60 minutes before eating.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; avoid if it aggravates upper GI symptoms.

serious: Severe esophagitis, esophageal ulcer/erosion, rarely stricture or perforation
Severe incapacitating bone, joint, or muscle pain

monitoring: Serum calcium and vitamin D; correct hypocalcemia and mineral disturbances before starting
Thigh/groin pain suggesting atypical femur fracture
Dental/oral status, especially before invasive dental procedures
Re-evaluate need for continued therapy periodically (after 3-5 years in low-risk patients)
counsel: Take exactly as directed: once monthly in the morning, on the same date each month, after an overnight fast
Swallow whole with a full glass (6-8 oz) of plain water; do not chew or suck the tablet
Stay upright (sitting or standing) for at least 60 minutes and do not eat, drink anything but plain water, or take other medicines during that time
Tell your doctor about new heartburn, difficulty or pain on swallowing, or chest pain, and about thigh or groin pain
Maintain good oral hygiene and tell your dentist you take a bisphosphonate; take calcium and vitamin D as advised but not within 60 minutes of the dose
pk: Reduction in bone turnover markers within ~1 month; BMD gain over months
Apparent terminal half-life ~37 to 157 hours for the 150 mg tablet
Prolonged skeletal retention supports once-monthly dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); dispense in a tight container
pearls: Oral bioavailability is very low (~0.6%) and abolished by food - strict fasting administration is essential
Not metabolized; eliminated unchanged renally, so no hepatic adjustment but avoid if CrCl <30 mL/min
Atypical femur fractures may present with prodromal dull thigh/groin pain weeks to months before; evaluate both limbs
Consider drug holiday after 3-5 years in patients at low fracture risk
Correct hypocalcemia and vitamin D deficiency before initiating
missed: If the missed once-monthly dose is more than 7 days before the next scheduled day, take one 150 mg tablet the morning after it is remembered, then return to the original monthly schedule. If the next scheduled day is only 1 to 7 days away, skip the missed dose and wait until the next scheduled day. Never take two 150 mg tablets within the same week.
overdose: No specific treatment exists. Oral overdose may cause hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper GI effects such as upset stomach, dyspepsia, esophagitis, gastritis, or ulcer. Give milk or antacids to bind the drug. Do not induce vomiting because of esophageal irritation risk, and keep the patient fully upright. Dialysis is not beneficial.
